pr.title: Ignore the build directory setuptools writes at the root
pr.head: a6bc4aecfef6c36f2f947d91e9b36b110d34a34b

summary: .gitignore tells Git which untracked files to leave out of git status and git add. Installing the Projector CLI from a checkout with pip install . makes setuptools, the Python build tool, write its build output to a build/ directory at the repository root: a copy of the package under build/lib/ and an empty build/bdist.<platform>/. The file already ignored setuptools' other output, *.egg-info/, but not build/, so every checkout that ever installed itself listed build/ as untracked.

This pull request adds one rule, /build/. The leading slash anchors it to the repository root. An unanchored build/ would match a directory of that name at any depth, and would silently hide a Projector plan named build, which would live at docs/projects/build/readme.md.

groups.title: Ignore the root build directory
groups.kicker: One anchored ignore rule beside the other setuptools output
intro: The new line sits beside *.egg-info/, under the file's opening comment that credentials and local build output never belong in the repository. It changes only what Git reports as untracked. Nothing in the repository reads .gitignore to decide what to package or publish.

files.note: Adds /build/, anchored to the root, so only setuptools' output directory is ignored.

checks.text: git check-ignore -v at this head matches build/lib/projector/cli.py and build/bdist.linux-x86_64/x to this line, and matches none of docs/projects/build/readme.md, site/build/x.js and hooks/build/x.

No tracked file sits under any build/ directory, so the rule hides nothing the repository commits. The wheel's contents do not depend on .gitignore: pyproject.toml lists its packages and package data explicitly. The full test suite, project check, and both claude plugin validate runs pass at this head.
